title: Static site generation (SSG) and incremental regeneration

videos.script:
The fastest page to serve is one that was finished before anybody asked for it. This lesson is about those pages. {{files}} You will render every page of the planner at build time, into files, and serve them with a server that knows nothing about courses.

{{four}} Then the four meta-frameworks do the same. Each one writes a file per page, and you will list the files to prove it.

{{stale}} Then the cost. Change the data, and the page goes on saying the old thing, with a perfectly good 200. {{time}} And a rebuild renders every page again, even the ones nobody touched.

{{isr}} The answer is to regenerate one page at a time. Next.js and Nuxt both do it, and you will watch the exact request that still gets the old page. {{demand}} Then on demand: an address that says the data changed, protected by a secret.

{{choose}} By the end you will be able to place any page on one line, from built once to rendered every time.
